Q: This is the adjuster speaking. The recording has started. Please state your full name for the file.
A: I'd rather just keep it to my first name for now, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were and what you were doing when the collision happened?
A: I was driivng on a two-lane road in Conroe, heading home from the store. It was a weekday afternoon and traffic
was light.
Q: What happened as you approached the point of impact?
A: The other car crossed into my lane while it was trying to pass a slow truck. I braked and steered to the right, but we
still met nose to nose. It wasn't a hard hit, though. Both cars were going slowly.
Q: Did either airbag deploy?
A: No, they didn't. I got out of the car on my own and walked around for a bit before I sat down on the curb.
Q: Did you feel any pain at the scene?
A: Not right away. About an hour later my neck got stiff and a dull ache started across my lower back. By that
evening, turning my head to check traffic was painful.
Q: Have you seen a doctor or other provider since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care the next morning. They diagnosed a neck and back strain, gave me muscle relaxers,
and told me to follow up with physical therapy.
Q: Have you had any prior injuries to your neck or back?
A: I had some stiffness years ago after a fall at work, but nothing that kept me from working or needed treatment in
the last several years.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I'm still having trouble sleeping and I've missed some shifts. I'm willing to provide my medical records.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the reocrded statement.
A: Thank you.
</page>

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
